notes.note: Courage at its very greatest - the kind that legends are made of.
Treats the refusal as rebelling against the people in charge - not just being difficult.

notes.note: Legal wording: the death is an event on a form.

notes.gloss: lacking conviction or boldness or courage
notes.note: Gently critical - the courage is missing, but the word feels sorry for the person more than it blames them.
Sounds a little like therapy talk; it names a kind of person rather than an act.
The participle points back at a sound original that errors have since entered, where *corrupt* simply reports the state.

notes.gloss: not having enough money to pay for necessities
notes.note: A refined word from books - it holds poverty at a polite distance.

notes.gloss: (used colloquially) having the relationship of friends or pals
notes.note: Openly mocking - the rhyming double sound carries the scorn for you.
The gentlest way to say *dead* - death softened into rest.
A gentler way to say *dead* - it softens the statement rather than praising the person.

notes.gloss: marked by or given to doubt
notes.note: Nearly neutral - it names the doubt without treating it as a fault.
A statement of possibility rather than of condition; nothing has been kept yet.

notes.gloss: marked by refinement in taste and manners
notes.note: Praises good taste and manners, but in a stiffly proper way - and it can carry a faint note of pity.
Formal, as at a ceremony - it lifts praise into the language of religious services.
The most scornful of the stubborn words - stubbornness treated as stupidity.
Like *flatter*, with gentle persuading added - the praise is a lever being pulled.
Idleness in a cool, Latin-sounding word - not wanting to make the effort, judged from above.
The sharpest edge in the group, hearing the fanaticism as belligerence rather than mere excess of zeal.

notes.gloss: pass from physical life and lose all bodily attributes and functions necessary to sustain life
notes.note: Even shorter and softer than *pass away* - the gentlest way of putting it.
Sounds heroic - a word at home in battle and legend.
